fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Moses goes up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and they saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24:9-10). Under His feet was “…a work like a pavement made of sapphire, as clear as the sky itself.” (Exodus 24:10). Moses and seventy-three others looking at that? I think nobody said a word.

You got it, baker. The LORD's list is Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders (Exodus 24:1). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Seventy people on one invitation? You know how hard it is to get a group chat to agree on a time? Now picture that with seventy elders.

Not quite, baker. Early the next morning Moses gets up and builds the altar at the base of the mountain, along with twelve pillars (Exodus 24:4). The going up comes later, when Moses goes up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders (Exodus 24:9). So the altar sits at the bottom, down where the people are.

Not the ground, friend. Moses puts half of the blood in bowls and splatters the other half on the altar (Exodus 24:6). I know the ground looks like a fair guess. I once aimed a spoonful of dough at the bowl and hit the floor, so I'm in no position to judge. The altar is where that second half goes.

Not this time, baker. The text says, “But God did not lay His hand on the nobles of Israel; they saw Him, and they ate and drank.” (Exodus 24:11). So God did not lay His hand on them. The verse moves right on to the eating and drinking.

Protection is a fair guess, friend. But the LORD says the tablets hold “…the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.” (Exodus 24:12). The word on the page is instruction, so these are written to teach the people.

Those two aren't in this verse, baker. Before heading up, Moses tells the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you.” (Exodus 24:14). Then he says, “Aaron and Hur are here with you. Whoever has a dispute can go to them.” So the names he gives are Aaron and Hur.

Eldad and Medad turn up later in Numbers 11:26, friend, but not here. In this verse Moses tells the elders, “Wait here for us until we return to you.” (Exodus 24:14). Then he says Aaron and Hur are with them, and whoever has a dispute can go to them.
